classification: Wrong IL business-use condition persisted B1--B6; first supplied positive-label counterexamples under an explicit public-text pattern occur in teacher13, not evidence of earlier ignored copies of these signals

EC_guidance.when: Illinois exemptions are allowable and the asset is debtor-owned personal property held for personal rather than business use.
EC_guidance.procedure: Check 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) independently for the asset and retain it alongside any applicable motor-vehicle, necessary-apparel, or prescribed-health-aid provision. Its $4,000 ceiling limits protected equity rather than EC eligibility.
EC_guidance.avoid_when: Do not apply § 12-1001(b) to real or business-use property. Do not classify jewelry as necessary wearing apparel under § 12-1001(a) merely because it is worn.

EV_guidance.when: Illinois exemptions are allowable and the asset is debtor-owned personal property used personally rather than for business.
EV_guidance.procedure: Include 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) independently alongside any applicable motor-vehicle, necessary-apparel, or prescribed-health-aid exemption. Protect up to $4,000 of each debtor's interest and sum the protected interests for the whole asset; under equal joint ownership this yields at most $8,000, subject to the asset's value.
EV_guidance.avoid_when: Do not apply § 12-1001(b) to real or business-use property, omit it because a specific exemption also applies, or classify a necklace, watch, or other jewelry as necessary wearing apparel under § 12-1001(a).

EC_guidance.when: Illinois exemptions are allowable and the asset is debtor-owned personal property used personally rather than for business.
EC_guidance.procedure: After classifying specific exemptions, make a separate § 12-1001(b) pass over every qualifying personal-property asset. Add 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) alongside any motor-vehicle, necessary-apparel or prescribed-health-aid citation, as well as for jewelry and other personal property. Its $4,000 ceiling limits protected equity, not EC eligibility.
EC_guidance.avoid_when: Do not apply § 12-1001(b) to real property or property the facts explicitly identify as business-use. Do not omit it because a specific exemption applies, and do not classify jewelry as necessary wearing apparel.

EV_guidance.when: Illinois exemptions are allowable and the asset is debtor-owned personal property used personally rather than for business.
EV_guidance.procedure: After all specific subsections, make a separate § 12-1001(b) pass over every such asset. The phrase “any other property” supplies an independent alternative even when apparel, motor-vehicle, or prescribed-health-aid protection also applies. Report the lesser of the whole asset's value and $4,000 for one debtor or $8,000 for two equal joint debtors.
EV_guidance.avoid_when: Do not apply § 12-1001(b) to real or explicitly business-use property, omit it because another subsection applies, or replace a specific exemption with it.

scope_limit: This is a literal public-description pattern over actual supplied teacher targets, not a semantic census of all possible business-purpose formulations or proof that no earlier indirect signal existed. Supplied statutes already said anyotherproperty; lack of these examples does not make the initial restriction legally supported.
interpretation: A learned unsupported restriction can persist until its counterexamples arrive; teacher13 actually proposes a generic condition correction. The completed112-source replay, not presence of a proposed correction, must establish benefit and harm.
